issues.legal_issue: Income from selling water pumped out of a mine is profit derived from the mine for purposes of assessing cess.
material_facts: Water accumulated in the mine and had to be pumped out to prevent inundation and enable the mine to operate.
The mine owner sold the pumped water to a neighbouring factory and received income from the sale.
The cess authorities included that income in the mine’s profits when assessing cess.
issues.conclusion: The sale income from the pumped water constituted profit derived from the mine and was assessable to cess.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 6 and 72 of the Bengal Cess Act, 1880 provide for cess on annual net profits from mines and for returns of those profits. Applying Tata Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. v. State of Bihar, [1963] Supp. 1 SCR 199, the Court held that profit derived from an activity connected with the mine is included; the principle applies directly where the pumped water is separately sold for a price.

rule.if: mine_cess_assessment_appeal and mine_water_pumped_for_operations and pumped_water_sold_for_price and income_received_from_water_sale

predicates.mine_cess_assessment_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a cess assessment based on profits derived from a mine.
predicates.mine_water_pumped_for_operations: Water accumulated in a mine and was pumped out to prevent inundation or enable the mine to operate.
predicates.pumped_water_sold_for_price: The mine operator sold the water pumped out of the mine for a price.
predicates.income_received_from_water_sale: The mine operator received income from selling the pumped water.

issues.definition: When a cess assessment appeal concerns income received from selling water pumped out of a mine for its operation, that sale income is treated as profit from the mine.

issues.legal_issue: The casual or irregular character of income from selling water pumped out of a mine does not exclude it from mine profits assessable to cess.
material_facts: The mine owner sold water pumped out of the mine and received income from the sale.
The owner argued that the income was casual rather than regular or permanent.
The income was assessed as profit derived from the mine.
issues.conclusion: The income was assessable even if it was casual, because the relevant provision did not distinguish between casual and regular income.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the Bengal Cess Act, 1880 makes no distinction between casual and regular income when defining profits from mines. The Court relied on its conclusion that income from selling water pumped out of a mine is profit derived from that mine.

rule.if: mine_cess_assessment_appeal and mine_water_pumped_for_operations and pumped_water_sold_for_price and income_received_from_water_sale and income_is_casual
